claim_records.text: The Nerfies method decomposes a non-rigidly deforming scene into a template volume represented as a neural radiance field (NeRF) and a per-observation deformation field that associates a point in observation coordinates to a point on the template.
Jointly optimizing a NeRF together with a deformation field leads to an under-constrained optimization problem.

fact_fields.method: Joint optimization of NeRF and deformation field

claim_records.text: Nerfies introduces an elastic regularization on the deformation, a background regularization, and a continuous coarse-to-fine annealing technique to address the under-constrained optimization problem and avoid bad local minima.

fact_fields.method: Elastic deformation regularization, background regularization, continuous coarse-to-fine annealing

claim_records.text: NeRF uses a neural network to encode color and density as a function of location and viewing angle, and generates novel views using volume rendering.

Nerfies generalizes NeRF by using a canonical NeRF model as a template for all observations, supplemented by a per-observation deformation field represented as an MLP conditioned on a per-image learned latent code that warps 3D points from observation coordinates to the canonical model frame.
A neural radiance field (NeRF) is a continuous volumetric function F: (x, d, ψi) → (c, σ) which maps a 3D position x and viewing direction d to a color c and density σ.

NeRF maps inputs x and d using a sinusoidal positional encoding γ: R3 → R3+6m defined as γ(x) = [x, ···, sin(2^k πx), cos(2^k πx), ···], where m is a hyper-parameter controlling the total number of frequency bands and k ∈ {0, ..., m−1}.

fact_fields.method: Sinusoidal positional encoding for NeRF inputs

claim_records.text: Coupled with volume rendering techniques, NeRFs can represent scenes with photo-realistic quality.

fact_fields.method: Neural Radiance Fields (NeRF) with volume rendering

claim_records.text: Nerfies is the first method capable of photorealistically reconstructing deformable scenes using photos/videos captured casually from mobile phones.
Nerfies augments NeRF by optimizing an additional continuous volumetric deformation field that warps each observed point into a canonical 5D NeRF.
NeRF-like deformation fields are prone to local minima, and Nerfies proposes a coarse-to-fine optimization method for coordinate-based models that allows for more robust optimization.

fact_fields.method: Coarse-to-fine optimization for coordinate-based deformable NeRF models

claim_records.text: Nerfies proposes an elastic regularization of the deformation field adapted from principles of geometry processing and physical simulation, which further improves optimization robustness.

fact_fields.method: Elastic deformation regularization adapted from geometry processing and physical simulation

claim_records.text: Nerfies can turn casually captured selfie photos/videos into deformable NeRF models that allow for photorealistic renderings of the subject from arbitrary viewpoints, which are dubbed "nerfies".
Nerfies evaluation uses time-synchronized data collected with a rig of two mobile phones, yielding train/validation images of the same pose at different viewpoints.

fact_fields.method: Data collection using two-mobile-phone synchronized rig

claim_records.text: Nerfies faithfully reconstructs non-rigidly deforming scenes and reproduces unseen views with high fidelity.

The Nerfies deformation network takes a position-encoded position γ_α(x) using coarse-to-fine annealing parameterized by α, along with a deformation code ω, and outputs a deformed position x′; its architecture is identical across all experiments.
The Nerfies canonical NeRF network is identical to the original NeRF MLP, except it provides an appearance latent code ψ along with the view direction to modulate appearance as in the NeRF-A model.
NSFF models dynamic scenes by directly conditioning NeRF with a position-encoded time variable γ(t), modulating color, density, and a scene-flow prediction.
Nerfies differs from NSFF in that Nerfies uses a deformation field while NSFF directly modulates NeRF density by conditioning it with γ(t).

fact_fields.method: Comparative analysis between Nerfies and NSFF

claim_records.text: Nerfies differs from NSFF in that Nerfies uses a per-example latent code to condition each observation while NSFF uses a position-encoded time variable γ(t).

fact_fields.method: Comparative analysis between Nerfies and NSFF

claims: The Nerfies method decomposes a non-rigidly deforming scene into a template volume represented as a neural radiance field (NeRF) and a per-observation deformation field that associates a point in observation coordinates to a point on the template.
Jointly optimizing a NeRF together with a deformation field leads to an under-constrained optimization problem.

Nerfies introduces an elastic regularization on the deformation, a background regularization, and a continuous coarse-to-fine annealing technique to address the under-constrained optimization problem and avoid bad local minima.
NeRF uses a neural network to encode color and density as a function of location and viewing angle, and generates novel views using volume rendering.

Nerfies generalizes NeRF by using a canonical NeRF model as a template for all observations, supplemented by a per-observation deformation field represented as an MLP conditioned on a per-image learned latent code that warps 3D points from observation coordinates to the canonical model frame.
A neural radiance field (NeRF) is a continuous volumetric function F: (x, d, ψi) → (c, σ) which maps a 3D position x and viewing direction d to a color c and density σ.

NeRF maps inputs x and d using a sinusoidal positional encoding γ: R3 → R3+6m defined as γ(x) = [x, ···, sin(2^k πx), cos(2^k πx), ···], where m is a hyper-parameter controlling the total number of frequency bands and k ∈ {0, ..., m−1}.
Coupled with volume rendering techniques, NeRFs can represent scenes with photo-realistic quality.
Nerfies is the first method capable of photorealistically reconstructing deformable scenes using photos/videos captured casually from mobile phones.
Nerfies augments NeRF by optimizing an additional continuous volumetric deformation field that warps each observed point into a canonical 5D NeRF.
NeRF-like deformation fields are prone to local minima, and Nerfies proposes a coarse-to-fine optimization method for coordinate-based models that allows for more robust optimization.
Nerfies proposes an elastic regularization of the deformation field adapted from principles of geometry processing and physical simulation, which further improves optimization robustness.
Nerfies can turn casually captured selfie photos/videos into deformable NeRF models that allow for photorealistic renderings of the subject from arbitrary viewpoints, which are dubbed "nerfies".
Nerfies evaluation uses time-synchronized data collected with a rig of two mobile phones, yielding train/validation images of the same pose at different viewpoints.
Nerfies faithfully reconstructs non-rigidly deforming scenes and reproduces unseen views with high fidelity.

The Nerfies deformation network takes a position-encoded position γ_α(x) using coarse-to-fine annealing parameterized by α, along with a deformation code ω, and outputs a deformed position x′; its architecture is identical across all experiments.
The Nerfies canonical NeRF network is identical to the original NeRF MLP, except it provides an appearance latent code ψ along with the view direction to modulate appearance as in the NeRF-A model.
NSFF models dynamic scenes by directly conditioning NeRF with a position-encoded time variable γ(t), modulating color, density, and a scene-flow prediction.
Nerfies differs from NSFF in that Nerfies uses a deformation field while NSFF directly modulates NeRF density by conditioning it with γ(t).
Nerfies differs from NSFF in that Nerfies uses a per-example latent code to condition each observation while NSFF uses a position-encoded time variable γ(t).
Nerfies differs from NSFF in that NSFF uses depth from MI-DAS and optical flow from RAFT as supervision while Nerfies only uses a photometric loss.
Nerfies uses the official code released by NSFF authors, with hyper-parameters tuned for Nerfies' datasets, for quantitative comparison with NSFF.
MS-SSIM metrics for the Nerfies evaluation are reported in Tab. 2.

claim_records.text: Existing Human NeRF methods for reconstructing 3D humans typically rely on multiple 2D images from multi-view cameras or monocular videos captured from fixed camera views.
Human images captured from random camera angles present challenges for high-quality 3D human reconstruction.
SHERF is the first generalizable Human NeRF model for recovering animatable 3D humans from a single input image.
SHERF extracts and encodes 3D human representations in canonical space, enabling rendering and animation from free views and poses.

fact_fields.method: SHERF canonical space 3D human representation encoding

claim_records.text: SHERF uses a bank of 3D-aware hierarchical features including global, point-level, and pixel-aligned features to facilitate informative encoding.
Global features in SHERF enhance the information extracted from the single input image and complement the information missing from the partial 2D observation.
Point-level features in SHERF provide strong clues of 3D human structure.
Pixel-aligned features in SHERF preserve more fine-grained details.
SHERF uses a feature fusion transformer to effectively integrate the 3D-aware hierarchical feature bank.

Extensive experiments on THuman, RenderPeople, ZJU_MoCap, and HuMMan datasets demonstrate that SHERF achieves state-of-the-art performance, with better generalizability for novel view and pose synthesis.

claim_records.text: The Explicit-NeRF-QA dataset uses 22 3D objects with diverse geometries, textures, and material complexities to train four typical explicit NeRF models across five parameter levels.
Lossy compression during Explicit-NeRF-QA model generation pivots on key parameters including hash table size for InstantNGP and voxel grid resolution for Plenoxels.
A large scale subjective experiment in a lab environment collected subjective scores from 21 viewers by rendering NeRF samples to processed video sequences (PVS).
The best Pearson correlation of around 0.85 is collected from the full-reference objective metric on the Explicit-NeRF-QA dataset.

claim_records.text: HyperNeRF lifts NeRFs into a higher dimensional space, representing the 5D radiance field for each input image as a slice through this hyper-space.
Compared to Nerfies, HyperNeRF reduces average error rates by 4.1% for interpolation as measured by LPIPS.
Compared to Nerfies, HyperNeRF reduces average error rates by 8.6% for novel-view synthesis as measured by LPIPS.
NeRF uses a conventional multilayer perceptron (MLP) to parameterize volumetric density and color as a function of spatial scene coordinates.

In NeRF, an analytical physics-based volumetric rendering engine is used to render a scene whose geometry and radiance are parameterized by a neural network, rather than using a neural network to directly render an image.

NeRF variants for dynamic scenes are separated into two categories: deformation-based approaches that apply spatially-varying deformation to a canonical radiance field, and modulation-based approaches that directly condition the radiance field on input image properties.

NeRF represents a scene as a continuous volumetric field of density and radiance, defined as function F: (x, d, ψi) → (c, σ) parameterized by an MLP, mapping 3D position x and viewing direction d to color c and density σ.
NeRF maps input coordinates x and d using sinusoidal positional encoding before providing them to the MLP.

HyperNeRF extends the domain of the template NeRF to a higher dimensional space (x, w) ∈ R^(3+W), where W is the number of higher dimensions, with the template NeRF represented as MLP F: (x, w, d, ψi) → (c, σ).
HyperNeRF associates a latent deformation code ωi and a latent appearance code ψi with each image i.

In HyperNeRF, samples x along rays are concatenated with the image's latent deformation code ωi and provided as input to MLPs parameterizing a deformation field, which yields a warped coordinate x' and a slicing surface in hyperspace that produces ambient coordinate w.

In HyperNeRF, the concatenation of (x', w), viewing direction d, and appearance code ψi are used as inputs to the MLP parameterizing the template NeRF, with densities and colors integrated along the ray via volumetric rendering.

claim_records.text: Deformable Neural Mesh Primitive (DNMP) is a flexible and compact neural variant of classic mesh representation that combines rasterization-based rendering efficiency with neural representation capability for photo-realistic image synthesis.
A DNMP consists of a set of connected deformable mesh vertices with paired vertex features to parameterize the geometry and radiance information of a local area.
DNMP enforces the shape of each primitive to be decoded from a relatively low-dimensional latent space to constrain optimization degrees of freedom and lower storage budgets.
DNMP rendering colors are decoded from vertex features interpolated with rasterization by a view-dependent MLP.
DNMP achieves leading performance for novel view synthesis in urban scenarios.
DNMP enables fast rendering at 2.07ms per 1k pixels.
DNMP has low peak memory usage of 110MB per 1k pixels.
The lightweight DNMP version runs 33 times faster than vanilla NeRFs.
The lightweight DNMP variant has rendering speed of 0.61ms per 1k pixels, comparable to highly-optimized Instant-NGP at 0.71ms per 1k pixels.

claim_records.text: 3DGS is introduced into indoor 3D Object Detection for the first time in this work.
3DGS primarily relies on 2D pixel-level supervision, resulting in unclear 3D spatial distribution of Gaussian blobs and poor differentiation between objects and background, which hinders indoor 3DOD.
2D images typically include numerous background pixels, leading to densely reconstructed 3DGS with many noisy Gaussian blobs representing the background, negatively affecting detection.
Incorporating 2D Boundary Guidance significantly enhances the spatial distribution of Gaussian blobs, resulting in clearer differentiation between objects and their background.

The Box-Focused Sampling strategy uses 2D boxes to generate object probability distribution in 3D space, allowing effective probabilistic sampling in 3D to retain more object blobs and reduce noisy background blobs.
3DGS-DET outperforms NeRF-Det++ by +6.0 on mAP@0.25 for the ScanNet dataset.
3DGS-DET outperforms NeRF-Det++ by +7.8 on mAP@0.5 for the ScanNet dataset.
3DGS-DET outperforms NeRF-Det++ by +14.9 on mAP@0.25 for the ARKITScenes dataset.

claim_records.text: NeRF operates exclusively on radiance (the product of reflectance and illumination) and does not explicitly perform scene decomposition into shape, reflectance and illumination.
NeRD, a NeRF extension, can perform reflectance decomposition but struggles to accurately recover detailed illumination, thereby significantly limiting realism.
The proposed reflectance decomposition network can estimate shape, BRDF, and per-image illumination given a set of object images captured under varying illumination.
Neural-PIL is an illumination integration network that replaces a costly illumination integral operation in the rendering with a simple network query.
Deep low-dimensional priors on BRDF and illumination representations are learned using novel smooth manifold auto-encoders.
The proposed decompositions result in considerably better BRDF and light estimates, enabling more accurate novel view-synthesis and relighting compared to prior art.

claim_records.text: Plenoxels represent a scene as a sparse 3D grid with spherical harmonics and can be optimized from calibrated images via gradient methods and regularization without any neural components.
On standard benchmark tasks, Plenoxels are optimized two orders of magnitude faster than Neural Radiance Fields with no loss in visual quality.
Plenoxels can render novel viewpoints at interactive rates of 15 fps with its non-fast-rendering-optimized implementation, and can be converted into a PlenOctree for faster rendering.
Direct optimization of Plenoxels' fully explicit 3D model achieves more than a 100× speedup over NeRF++ for training, reducing training time to roughly 4 days for NeRF++ baseline.

NeRF requires several days for full training and about half a minute to render a full image, because every rendered pixel requires evaluating the coordinate-based MLP at hundreds of sample locations along the corresponding ray.
NeRF's training lasts more than a day and rendering requires 30 seconds per frame on a single GPU.

Plenoxels is an explicit volumetric representation based on a view-dependent sparse voxel grid without any neural networks, optimized end-to-end from calibrated 2D photographs using differentiable rendering loss on training views and a total variation regularizer.
PlenOctrees extract a NeRF variant into a sparse voxel grid in which each voxel represents view-dependent color using spherical harmonics.
Both JAXNeRF and Plenoxel models exhibit artifacts in the synthetic drums scene, but the specific artifacts differ, with some artifacts unavoidable for any underdetermined inverse problem.

claim_records.text: NeuDA is a flexible neural implicit representation leveraging hierarchical voxel grids for high-fidelity surface reconstruction.
NeuDA maintains hierarchical anchor grids where each vertex stores a 3D position (or anchor) instead of a direct embedding (or feature).
NeuDA optimizes anchor grids such that different local geometry structures can be adaptively encoded.
NeuDA introduces a simple hierarchical positional encoding method for the hierarchical anchor structure to flexibly exploit properties of high-frequency and low-frequency geometry and appearance.
Experiments on the DTU and BlendedMVS datasets demonstrate that NeuDA can produce promising mesh surfaces.

claim_records.text: HollowNeRF delivers comparable rendering quality to Instant-NGP while utilizing just 31% of the parameters.
HollowNeRF can achieve a PSNR accuracy gain of up to 1dB using only 56% of the parameters.

HollowNeRF trains a coarse 3D saliency mask that guides efficient feature pruning, and employs an alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) pruner to sparsify the 3D saliency mask during training.
By exploiting sparsity in the 3D scene to redistribute hash collisions, HollowNeRF improves rendering quality while using a fraction of the parameters of comparable state-of-the-art solutions.

Existing hashgrid-based NeRF solutions for culling unnecessary feature grid regions rely on prior knowledge of object shape or periodically estimate object shape during training via repeated model evaluations, which are costly and wasteful.

claim_records.text: The explicit 3D Gaussian volume compression model achieves significant training speed and reconstruction quality improvements on both structured and unstructured volumes compared to existing INRs.
The explicit 3D Gaussian volume compression model enables compression ratios much higher than previous work for unstructured volumes.
Existing INRs for unstructured volumes do not encode geometry, requiring partial mesh storage for later sampling and limiting achievable compression.
The explicit 3D Gaussian volume model naturally encodes domain geometry, eliminating the need for mesh storage in unstructured volumes and introducing significantly higher compression opportunities.
The explicit 3D Gaussian volume model uses a sampling strategy that reconstructs scalar values at spatial locations through weighted aggregation of intersecting Gaussians.

The explicit 3D Gaussian volume model includes optimized CUDA-accelerated pipelines for structured and unstructured model sampling, loss functions that encourage accurate domain coverage, and a novel sampling-error based densification strategy.

claim_records.text: Most prior neural rendering works following the original NeRF require an expensive per-scene optimization process.
MVSNeRF leverages deep MVS techniques to achieve across-scene neural radiance field estimation for view synthesis using only few images as input.
MVSNeRF's entire framework models a neural radiance field, regressing volume density and view-dependent radiance in the scene from few (three) input images.
Once the scene encoding volume S is reconstructed, this volume combined with the MLP decoder A can be used independently without the prepending 2D and 3D CNNs.

MVSNeRF reconstructs a neural encoding volume and regresses volume density and view-dependent radiance at arbitrary points in a scene, enabling applying differentiable volume rendering to regress images colors.
The physically based volume rendering equation can be numerically evaluated via differentiable ray marching for view synthesis.
A pixel's radiance value (color) is computed by marching a ray through the pixel and accumulating radiance at sampled shading points on the ray.
MVSNeRF as a radiance field function provides the volume rendering properties σk and rk for the ray marching.
The ray marching rendering in MVSNeRF is fully differentiable, allowing the framework to regress final pixel colors at novel viewpoints using the three input views from end to end.
MVSNeRF supervises its entire framework with groundtruth pixel colors using an L2 rendering loss.
MVSNeRF estimates a neural scene encoding volume that consists of per-voxel neural features encoding information about the local scene geometry and appearance.
MVSNeRF uses a multi-layer perceptron (MLP) to decode the volume density and radiance at arbitrary continuous locations using tri-linearly interpolated neural features inside the encoding volume.
Once estimated, the encoding volume can be used directly (dropping the 3D CNN) for final rendering by differentiable ray marching.
Compared with existing MVS methods, MVSNeRF enables differentiable neural rendering that allows for training without 3D supervision and inference time optimization for further quality improvement.

input.query: Explain the foundational NeRF representation and differentiable volume-rendering formulation.

claim_records.text: RayGauss achieves inference speeds of 25 FPS on the Blender dataset.

RayGauss provides a physically consistent formulation of emitted radiance c and density σ, decomposed with Gaussian functions associated with Spherical Gaussians/Harmonics for all-frequency colorimetric representation.
RayGauss introduces a method enabling differentiable ray casting of irregularly distributed Gaussians using an algorithm that integrates radiance fields slab by slab and leverages a BVH structure.
RayGauss achieves superior rendering quality compared to the state-of-the-art while maintaining reasonable training times.
RayGauss represents radiance fields as a weighted sum of locally supported elliptical basis functions with optimizable positions, orientations, and scales.
RayGauss combines spherical harmonics (SH) and spherical Gaussians (SG) with elliptical basis functions to better represent high-frequency color variations such as specular reflections.
RayGauss's Volume Raycasting algorithm avoids splatting artifacts such as flickering.

RayGauss's ray casting algorithm for sparse basis functions sequentially integrates the radiance field slab-by-slab, accumulating colorimetric properties along the ray in slabs of space corresponding to multiple samples rather than processing individual samples.
RayGauss's ray casting algorithm and its backpropagation rely on a Bounding Volume Hierarchy (BVH) implemented on GPU with the OptiX library.
NeRF uses a differentiable Volume Ray Casting algorithm that launches rays in 3D space to compute a discretized version of the volumetric rendering equation using N samples along the ray.

claim_records.text: NeRFMeshing distills a trained NeRF volumetric 3D representation into a Signed Surface Approximation Network, enabling easy extraction of a physically accurate 3D mesh and appearance that can be rendered in real time on an array of devices.
NeRFMeshing introduces a signed surface approximation network (SSAN) that estimates a Truncated Signed Distance Field (TSDF) and a feature appearance field.
NeRFMeshing can be leveraged together with any NeRF, without requiring modifications to the NeRF architecture.
NeRFMeshing produces meshes with neural colors having accurate geometry that can be rendered in real time on commodity hardware.
NeRFMeshing does not rely on a fixed grid template during training, enabling reconstruction at any arbitrary resolution afterwards.
NeRFMeshing relies on NeRF networks trained from images, without requiring additional input modalities such as depth.
NeRFMeshing extracts meshes from scenes including Chair, Hot-dog, Lego from the Blender dataset and Garden from the MipNeRF 360 dataset.

claim_records.text: The NeRF method represents a scene using a fully-connected non-convolutional deep network that takes a single continuous 5D coordinate (spatial location (x,y,z) and viewing direction (θ, φ)) as input and outputs volume density and view-dependent emitted radiance at that spatial location.

fact_fields.method: NeRF continuous volumetric scene function optimization

claim_records.text: NeRF synthesizes novel views by querying 5D coordinates along camera rays and using classic volume rendering techniques to project output colors and densities into an image.

fact_fields.method: Differentiable volume rendering for view synthesis

claim_records.text: NeRF represents a continuous scene as a 5D vector-valued function whose input is a 3D location x=(x,y,z) and 2D viewing direction (θ,φ), and whose output is an emitted color c=(r,g,b) and volume density σ.

NeRF optimizes a deep fully-connected neural network without any convolutional layers (MLP) to represent the 5D scene function by regressing from a single 5D coordinate (x,y,z,θ,φ) to a single volume density and view-dependent RGB color.

NeRF's technical contributions include an approach for representing continuous scenes with complex geometry and materials as 5D neural radiance fields parameterized as basic MLP networks, a differentiable rendering procedure based on classical volume rendering, and a positional encoding to map input 5D coordinates into a higher dimension.
The synthetic Drums scene NeRF visualization uses a set of 100 input views randomly captured on a surrounding hemisphere.

fact_fields.method: NeRF input view capture for synthetic scene

claim_records.text: A model trained without view dependence (only x as input) has difficulty representing specularities, while the full NeRF model uses input viewing direction passed to an additional fully-connected layer with ReLU activation and 128 channels to output view-dependent RGB color.

The expected color C(r) of camera ray r(t)=o+td with near and far bounds tn and tf is computed via volume rendering as C(r) = ∫_{tn}^{tf} T(t)σ(r(t))c(r(t),d)dt, where T(t) = exp(-∫_{tn}^{t} σ(r(s))ds).

claim_records.text: MobileNeRF is represented as a set of polygons with textures representing binary opacities and feature vectors, rendered using traditional polygon rasterization with a z-buffer to produce per-pixel features interpreted by a small view-dependent MLP running in a fragment shader to produce final pixel color.

fact_fields.method: MobileNeRF textured polygon representation with fragment shader MLP

claim_records.text: Traditional NeRF implementations use a volumetric rendering algorithm that evaluates a large MLP at hundreds of sample positions along the ray for each pixel to estimate and integrate density and radiance, making the rendering process far too slow for interactive visualization.

SNeRG's precomputation and deferred rendering approach increases the rendering speed of NeRF by three orders of magnitude, but still relies upon ray marching through a sparse voxel grid and requires a significant amount of GPU memory to store volumetric textures, prohibiting it from running on common mobile devices.

fact_fields.method: SNeRG sparse voxel grid precomputation and deferred rendering

claim_records.text: MobileNeRF's rendering pipeline does not sample rays or sort polygons in depth order, and thus can model only binary opacities.
MobileNeRF is 10× faster than SNeRG with the same output quality on standard test scenes.

fact_fields.method: MobileNeRF vs SNeRG rendering speed comparison

claim_records.text: MobileNeRF consumes less memory than SNeRG by storing surface textures instead of volumetric textures, enabling the method to run on integrated GPUs with limited memory and power.

MobileNeRF runs on a web browser and is compatible with all tested devices, as its viewer is an HTML webpage, and allows real-time manipulation of reconstructed objects/scenes as they are simple triangle meshes.
Light fields and Lumigraphs store a dense grid of images enabling real-time rendering of high quality scenes, albeit with limited camera freedom and significant storage overhead.

Point-based representations that refine scene geometry while training post-processing networks often result in a lack of 3D consistency, require powerful desktop GPUs, and have not been demonstrated to run on a mobile device.

fact_fields.method: Point-based neural rendering with post-processing CNN

claim_records.text: DefTet differentiably renders a tetrahedral grid with occupancy and color at each vertex, then composites interpolated values at all intersected faces along a ray, incurring a significant loss in view-synthesis quality.

NVDiffRec combines differentiable marching tetrahedra with differentiable rasterization to perform full inverse rendering and extract triangle meshes, materials, and lighting from images, enabling elaborate editing and scene relighting, but incurs a significant loss in view-synthesis quality.
Rendering a NeRF involves evaluating a large neural network at multiple 3D locations per pixel, preventing real-time rendering.

claim_records.text: Progressive Volume Distillation (PVD) is a systematic distillation method that enables any-to-any conversions between different NeRF architectures, including MLP, sparse or low-rank tensors, hashtables and their compositions.
PVD performs distillation progressively on different levels of volume representations, from shallower to deeper, to enable fast architecture conversions.

With PVD, an MLP-based NeRF model distilled from a hashtable-based Instant-NGP model achieves a 10×~20× faster speed than training the original NeRF from scratch, while achieving superior synthesis quality.
Hashtable-based NeRF representations admit faster training and rendering but their lack of clear geometric meaning hampers downstream tasks like spatial-relation-aware editing.
PVD employs special treatment of density to deal with its specific numerical instability problem during distillation.

A NeRF model distilled by PVD from an INGP teacher within 1.5 hours achieves improved synthesis quality compared to a NeRF model trained from scratch using 25 hours on the Family and Barn scene from TanksAndTemples dataset.
Instant Neural Graphics Primitives (INGP) utilizes multilevel hash tables for effective compression of feature tensors.

Methods with explicit or hybrid NeRF representations usually enjoy faster training due to shallower representations and cope better with geometric-aware editing like merging and other scene manipulations, in contrast to purely implicit representations.

PVD builds a block-wise distillation strategy to accelerate the training procedure based on a unified view of different NeRF architectures, and employs special treatment of the dynamic density volume range by clipping to improve training stability and synthesis quality.
Distillation from hashtable and VM-decomposition structures often helps boost student model synthesis quality and consumes less time than training from scratch.

claim_records.text: NeRF generates a volumetric radiance field representation that creates color and density for every point within the relevant 3D space, rather than directly restoring the whole 3D scene geometry.

CAMPARI simultaneously learns a camera generator and an image generator, enabling use of complex camera distributions without manual tuning, and represents scenes via foreground and background decomposition for 3D-consistent representations and accurate camera distribution recovery.
Pix2NeRF introduces a pipeline to generate NeRF from a single input image, built upon π-GAN, and employs an unsupervised approach that can be trained with independent images.
Pix2NeRF is currently restricted to work with only one category per dataset, impeding its ability to generalize to new categories.

NeRF uses a deep neural network to represent complex scenes in a fully connected, non-convolutional way, taking a continuous 5D coordinate as input and outputting volume density and view-dependent emitted radiance at that spatial location.
NeRF uses classic volume rendering techniques to synthesize views and is optimized using a set of images with known camera poses.

NeRF introduces positional encoding and a hierarchical sampling strategy to address the inefficiency of the basic implementation, and can represent non-Lambertian effects such as specularities using input viewing direction.

claim_records.text: The proposed single-view volumetric field reconstruction technique models the unknown distribution of volumetric fields using an unconditional diffusion model trained on a novel benchmark dataset of 1,000 synthetically simulated volumetric density fields.

fact_fields.method: unconditional diffusion model for volumetric field distribution modeling

claim_records.text: The neural diffusion model is trained on the latent codes of a novel, diffusion-friendly, monoplanar representation.

fact_fields.method: diffusion model training on monoplanar representation latent codes

claim_records.text: A physically-based differentiable volume renderer is employed to provide gradients with respect to light transport in the latent space, making reconstructions better aligned with observed data compared to classic NeRF approaches.

The reconstruction of internal density distribution of highly dense volumes is nearly impossible due to high uncertainty in the light scattering process and presence of vanishing gradients, and this limitation can only be alleviated by incorporating prior information during reconstruction.

The proposed approach employs a diffusion prior to guide a Physically-based Differentiable Volume Renderer (PDVR) toward reconstructing a plausible volumetric field, with controlled variations in the diffusion step by considering the gradient of the image loss with respect to the learned latent space representation.

fact_fields.method: diffusion prior-guided Physically-based Differentiable Volume Renderer (PDVR)

claim_records.text: The diffusion model is trained on a dataset of 1,000 synthetically simulated volumetric density fields (cumulus clouds in the case study), using a novel diffusion-friendly representation for decoding.

fact_fields.method: diffusion model training on synthetic volumetric density fields

claim_records.text: The renderer is coupled with the diffusion model to reconstruct radiance parameters using the prior for the density distribution but not for its appearance, so the 3D density field can be trained solely on the prior without requiring images of all possible backgrounds and light scattering effects.
The work contributes a large database of 3D cumulus cloud-like density fields generated using numerical fluid simulation.

fact_fields.method: numerical fluid simulation for density field generation

claim_records.text: The work contributes a 3D cloud decoder utilizing a novel, diffusion-friendly monoplanar representation, trained jointly on a subset of the database.

fact_fields.method: 3D cloud decoder with diffusion-friendly monoplanar representation

claim_records.text: The work contributes a novel Parametric Diffusion Posterior Sampling (PDPS) technique utilizing a shape-centric prior with a physically-based differentiable volume renderer, and is the first approach that integrates an unconditional diffusion model trained on volumetric density distributions with a differentiable volume renderer.
The approach is demonstrated across tasks including single- and multi-view reconstruction, and volume super-resolution.

claims: The proposed single-view volumetric field reconstruction technique models the unknown distribution of volumetric fields using an unconditional diffusion model trained on a novel benchmark dataset of 1,000 synthetically simulated volumetric density fields.
The neural diffusion model is trained on the latent codes of a novel, diffusion-friendly, monoplanar representation.

A physically-based differentiable volume renderer is employed to provide gradients with respect to light transport in the latent space, making reconstructions better aligned with observed data compared to classic NeRF approaches.

The reconstruction of internal density distribution of highly dense volumes is nearly impossible due to high uncertainty in the light scattering process and presence of vanishing gradients, and this limitation can only be alleviated by incorporating prior information during reconstruction.

The proposed approach employs a diffusion prior to guide a Physically-based Differentiable Volume Renderer (PDVR) toward reconstructing a plausible volumetric field, with controlled variations in the diffusion step by considering the gradient of the image loss with respect to the learned latent space representation.

The diffusion model is trained on a dataset of 1,000 synthetically simulated volumetric density fields (cumulus clouds in the case study), using a novel diffusion-friendly representation for decoding.

The renderer is coupled with the diffusion model to reconstruct radiance parameters using the prior for the density distribution but not for its appearance, so the 3D density field can be trained solely on the prior without requiring images of all possible backgrounds and light scattering effects.
The work contributes a large database of 3D cumulus cloud-like density fields generated using numerical fluid simulation.
The work contributes a 3D cloud decoder utilizing a novel, diffusion-friendly monoplanar representation, trained jointly on a subset of the database.

The work contributes a novel Parametric Diffusion Posterior Sampling (PDPS) technique utilizing a shape-centric prior with a physically-based differentiable volume renderer, and is the first approach that integrates an unconditional diffusion model trained on volumetric density distributions with a differentiable volume renderer.
The approach is demonstrated across tasks including single- and multi-view reconstruction, and volume super-resolution.

claim_records.text: Experiments on both synthetic and real-world datasets show Hyb-NeRF achieves faster rendering speed with better rendering quality and lower memory footprint compared to previous state-of-the-art methods.
On the ficus scene in Blender, Hyb-NeRF with 16.4M parameters achieves 35.85 PSNR and 0.986 SSIM, outperforming JNGP with 24.4M parameters which achieves 33.23 PSNR and 0.981 SSIM.

Hash-based multi-resolution grid representation has trainable features at coarse resolution levels with lower resolutions and less compression than fine-level feature grids, resulting in limited representation power and low memory efficiency.

fact_fields.method: analysis of hash-based multi-resolution grid representation properties

claim_records.text: All Hyb-NeRF models can reconstruct high-quality radiance fields in 9 minutes.

The smallest Hyb-NeRF model with 8.4M trainable parameters takes 4 minutes to achieve better rendering quality than state-of-the-art methods while requiring substantially less memory than previous and concurrent voxel-based methods.

claim_records.text: Mip-NeRF matches the accuracy of a brute-force supersampled NeRF on the presented multiscale dataset while being 22× faster.

Mip-NeRF reasons about the 3D conical frustum defined by a camera pixel and featurizes it using integrated positional encoding (IPE), which approximates the frustum with a multivariate Gaussian and computes the closed-form integral E[γ(x)] over positional encodings of coordinates within the Gaussian.

fact_fields.method: integrated positional encoding (IPE) over conical frustum

claim_records.text: NeRF training minimizes the sum of squared differences between all input pixel values and all predicted pixel values using gradient descent, and trains two separate MLPs (coarse and fine) to improve sample efficiency.

Mip-NeRF extends NeRF to represent the scene at a continuously-valued scale by efficiently rendering anti-aliased conical frustums instead of rays, reducing objectionable aliasing artifacts and improving fine detail representation.
Mip-NeRF is 7% faster than NeRF and has half the size of NeRF.
Compared to NeRF, mip-NeRF reduces average error rates by 17% on the dataset presented with NeRF.
Compared to NeRF, mip-NeRF reduces average error rates by 60% on a challenging multiscale variant of the NeRF dataset.
Mip-NeRF merges the separate coarse and fine MLPs used by NeRF for hierarchical sampling into a single MLP, resulting in approximately 7% faster speed than NeRF and half as many parameters.

IPE preserves frequencies that are constant over an interval and softly removes frequencies that vary over an interval, effectively producing anti-aliased positional encoding features that smoothly encode the size and shape of a volume of space.
For each pixel being rendered, mip-NeRF casts a cone instead of a ray, samples n+1 values for t_k, and computes IPE features for the interval spanning each adjacent pair of sampled t_k values.
NeRF's rendering model can cause excessive blurring and aliasing because it casts a single ray through each pixel and queries an MLP at samples along that ray.

claim_records.text: Fourier PlenOctrees suffer from artifacts introduced by involved compression when combined with recent state-of-the-art techniques for training static per-frame NeRF models.

The proposed FPO++ density encoding adapts Fourier-based compression to the characteristics of the transfer function used by the underlying volume rendering procedure, leading to a substantial reduction of artifacts in the dynamic model.
FPO++ augments training data to relax the periodicity assumption of the Fourier compression used in Fourier PlenOctrees.
PlenOctrees use a hierarchical octree structure of density and view-dependent radiance in terms of spherical harmonics (SH) to entirely avoid network evaluations during rendering.
Instant-NGP incorporated a multi-resolution hash encoding to significantly accelerate the training of neural models including NeRF.
Prior discrete scene representation acceleration methods including Instant-NGP, Plenoxels, and TensoRF are limited to static scenes only and do not account for dynamic scenarios like motion.
NeRF synthesizes novel views using volume rendering of density and view-dependent radiance optimized in an implicit neural scene representation using MLPs from a set of posed images.
Some NeRF variants reduce aliasing artifacts by modeling volumetric rendering with conical frustums instead of rays.
Fourier PlenOctrees (FPO) extend ordinary PlenOctrees by combining them with the Fourier transform, enabling efficient handling of time-variant density and SH-based radiance for dynamic scenes.
During FPO construction, compression is performed on encoded densities σ' = e_comp(e_log(σ)), where the encoding consists of a component-dependent part and a logarithmic part.

The proposed component-dependent and logarithmic density encoding allows better reconstruction of original densities without fine-tuning than can be achieved with only DFT and IDFT as used in standard FPO.

fact_fields.method: component-dependent + logarithmic density encoding vs DFT/IDFT only

claim_records.text: The logarithmic density encoding is defined as e_log(σ) = log(σ + 1), chosen so that e_log remains a non-negative function for non-negative input densities with e_log(0) = 0.
The logarithmic density encoding focuses Fourier approximation on densities near or equal to zero, since larger density values are mapped closer together while smaller values stay almost the same.

After applying the inverse of the logarithmic encoding after IDFT during rendering, the L2-error in fine-tuning is allowed to be larger for encoded high density values than without logarithmic encoding, focusing optimization on more important reconstruction parts.

claim_records.text: NerfDiff distills knowledge from a 3D-aware conditional diffusion model (CDM) into NeRF by synthesizing and refining a set of virtual views at test time.
NerfDiff significantly outperforms existing NeRF-based and geometry-free approaches on the ShapeNet, ABO, and Clevr3D datasets.
NerfDiff jointly trains a camera-space triplane-based NeRF together with a 3D-aware conditional diffusion model (CDM) on a collection of scenes at the training stage.
A naive finetuning strategy that optimizes NeRF parameters directly using CDM outputs leads to subpar renderings because CDM outputs tend to be multi-view inconsistent.

fact_fields.method: naive NeRF finetuning using CDM outputs

claim_records.text: NerfDiff's NeRF-guided distillation updates the NeRF representation and guides the multi-view diffusion process in an alternating fashion.
NerfDiff introduces an efficient image-conditioned NeRF representation based on camera-aligned triplanes that enables efficient rendering and finetuning from the CDM.
NerfDiff's 3D-aware CDM integrates volume rendering into 2D diffusion models to facilitate generalization to novel views.
Diffusion-based generative models have become state-of-the-art on image synthesis tasks.
Existing generalizable NeRF models conditioned by projection of 3D points and gathering of corresponding image features yield blurry results when target views are far from the input view.

fact_fields.method: generalizable NeRF models conditioned on projected 3D point image features

claim_records.text: NeRF requires tens or hundreds of images for overfitting a scene and has no generalization ability to infer new scenes.
Existing approaches leveraging 2D generative models to predict novel views conditioned on an input view are only able to synthesize partially 3D-consistent images.

fact_fields.method: 2D generative model-based novel view synthesis conditioned on input view

EvaSurf can run on mobile devices at over 40 FPS.
The final rendering package required for EvaSurf takes up only 40-50 MB.

EvaSurf uses a lightweight neural shader with explicit geometry and implicit texture to support real-time rendering on common mobile devices.

EvaSurf runs on common devices including PCs, tablets, and mobile phones with over 40 FPS.

claim_records.text: Neural Radiance Fields (NeRF) achieves impressive view synthesis results for 360° capture of bounded scenes and forward-facing capture of bounded and unbounded scenes.

NeRF fits multi-layer perceptrons (MLPs) representing view-invariant opacity and view-dependent color volumes to a set of training images, and samples novel views based on volume rendering techniques.
The NeRF++ method improves view synthesis fidelity for 360° captures of objects within large-scale, unbounded 3D scenes by addressing a parametrization issue.
An artificially constructed shape-radiance ambiguity solution is a valid NeRF reconstruction that perfectly fits input images but has very limited novel view synthesis ability.
Accurately generating a novel view from the degenerate shape-radiance ambiguity solution would require reconstructing an arbitrarily complex view-dependent function at each surface point.

The degenerate shape-radiance ambiguity model is very unlikely to accurately interpolate the complex view-dependent function unless training views are extremely dense, as in conventional light field rendering works.

NeRF avoids degenerate shape-radiance ambiguity solutions due to two related factors: incorrect geometry forces the radiance field to have higher intrinsic complexity, and NeRF's specific MLP structure implicitly encodes a smooth BRDF prior on surface reflectance.
As opacity σ deviates from the correct shape, radiance c must generally become a high-frequency function with respect to viewing direction d to reconstruct input images.
For the correct shape, the surface light field will generally be much smoother, and constant for Lambertian materials.
The higher complexity required for incorrect shapes is more difficult to represent with a limited capacity MLP.
NeRF's specific MLP structure encodes an implicit prior favoring smooth surface reflectance functions where radiance c is smooth with respect to viewing direction d at any given surface point x.

NeRF's MLP treats scene position x and viewing direction d asymmetrically: d is injected close to the end of the MLP, resulting in fewer MLP parameters and fewer non-linear activations involved in creating view-dependent effects.
In NeRF, the opacity field σ is computed as a function of 3D position x ∈ R³, and the radiance field c is parameterized by both 3D position x and viewing direction d ∈ S².

Replacing NeRF's radiance field model c with a vanilla MLP that treats x and d symmetrically (accepting both as inputs to the first layer and encoding both with γ₁₀(·)) results in reduced test image quality compared with NeRF's special MLP on DTU scenes.

claim_records.text: NeRF yields blurred rendering results when training images are captured at non-uniform scales.
NeRF produces aliasing artifacts if test images are taken in distant views.

Mip-NeRF proposes a multiscale representation as a conical frustum to encode scale information, but is only suitable for offline rendering since it relies on integrated positional encoding (IPE) to query a multilayer perceptron (MLP).

Mip-VoG is an explicit multiscale representation with a deferred architecture for real-time anti-aliasing rendering, including a density Mip-VoG for scene geometry and a feature Mip-VoG with a small MLP for view-dependent color.

Mip-VoG encodes scene scale using the level of detail (LOD) derived from ray differentials and uses quadrilinear interpolation to map a queried 3D location to its features and density from two neighboring downsampled voxel grids.
Mip-VoG is the first approach to offer multiscale training and real-time anti-aliasing rendering simultaneously.
Experiments on multiscale datasets show that Mip-VoG outperforms state-of-the-art real-time rendering baselines.

claim_records.text: pixelNeRF is a learning framework that predicts a continuous neural scene representation conditioned on one or few input images.
pixelNeRF introduces an architecture that conditions a NeRF on image inputs in a fully convolutional manner.
pixelNeRF can perform novel view synthesis in a feed-forward manner from a sparse set of views, as few as one.
pixelNeRF can be trained directly from images with no explicit 3D supervision, leveraging the volume rendering approach of NeRF.

pixelNeRF outperforms current state-of-the-art baselines for novel view synthesis and single image 3D reconstruction on ShapeNet benchmarks for held-out objects and entire unseen categories, multi-object ShapeNet scenes, and real scenes from the DTU dataset.
pixelNeRF outperforms current state-of-the-art baselines for novel view synthesis and single image 3D reconstruction on multi-object ShapeNet scenes and real scenes from the DTU dataset.
NeRF encodes a scene as a continuous volumetric radiance field f that returns a differential density σ and RGB color c for a 3D point x and viewing direction unit vector d.
The NeRF volumetric radiance field is rendered into a 2D image via the integral ˆC(r) = ∫ tf tn T(t)σ(t)c(t)dt, where T(t) = exp(−∫ t tn σ(s) ds) handles occlusion.
In pixelNeRF, the world point x with view direction d is transformed into each input view i's coordinate system using the world to camera transform as x(i) = P(i)x, d(i) = R(i)d.
In pixelNeRF, each input image is encoded into feature volume W(i) = E(I(i)), and the corresponding image feature is extracted at the projected image coordinate π(x(i)) for the view-space point x(i).

In pixelNeRF, intermediate vectors V(i) = f1(γ(x(i)), d(i); W(i) ◦ π(x(i))) are aggregated with average pooling operator ψ and passed into final layers f2 to obtain predicted density and color (σ, c) = f2(ψ(V(1), ..., V(n))).
Running each of 60 NeRFs took 14 hours, while pixelNeRF is applied to new scenes immediately without any test-time optimization.
pixelNeRF's rendering time increases linearly when given more input views.
Like vanilla NeRF, pixelNeRF requires manually tuning ray sampling bounds tn, tf and a scale for the positional encoding.
pixelNeRF's applicability is limited to datasets such as ShapeNet and DTU due to bottleneck from availability of large-scale wide baseline multi-view datasets.

claim_records.text: CLIP-NeRF is a multi-modal 3D object manipulation method for neural radiance fields that leverages the joint language-image embedding space of the CLIP model.
CLIP-NeRF allows manipulating NeRF using either a short text prompt or an exemplar image.
CLIP-NeRF introduces a disentangled conditional NeRF architecture that allows individual control over both shape and appearance.
In CLIP-NeRF, shape conditioning is achieved via applying a learned deformation field to the positional encoding, and color conditioning is deferred to the volumetric rendering stage.

CLIP-NeRF designs two code mappers that take a CLIP embedding as input and update the latent codes to reflect the targeted editing, trained with a CLIP-based matching loss to ensure manipulation accuracy.
CLIP-NeRF proposes an inverse optimization method that accurately projects an input image to the latent codes for manipulation to enable editing on real images.

claim_records.text: Tetra-NeRF uses an adaptive tetrahedral representation obtained via Delaunay triangulation, built on an available sparse point cloud of the scene, instead of uniform voxel subdivision or point-based representations.
The tetrahedral representation used by Tetra-NeRF enables efficient training and leads to state-of-the-art results.
Compared to voxel-based NeRF representations, Tetra-NeRF's tetrahedral representation provides more detail around scene parts likely to be close to the surface.
Compared to point-based NeRF representations, Tetra-NeRF's tetrahedral approach achieves better performance.

claim_records.text: UE4-NeRF partitions each large scene into different sub-NeRFs to support real-time rendering of large-scale scenes.

For each partitioned independent scene, UE4-NeRF initializes polygonal meshes by constructing multiple regular octahedra within the scene, with polygonal face vertices continuously optimized during training.
Drawing inspiration from Level of Detail (LOD) techniques, UE4-NeRF trains meshes of varying levels of detail for different observation levels.
Combined with the rasterization pipeline in Unreal Engine 4 (UE4), UE4-NeRF achieves real-time rendering of large-scale scenes at 4K resolution with a frame rate of up to 43 FPS.
Rendering within UE4 facilitates subsequent-stage scene editing for UE4-NeRF.
Experiments demonstrate that UE4-NeRF achieves rendering quality comparable to state-of-the-art approaches.

claim_records.text: NeRF trains a deep network to map 5D input coordinates representing spatial location and viewing direction into a volume density and view-dependent emitted radiance.
NeRF is only applicable to static scenes where the same spatial location can be queried from different images.

D-NeRF extends neural radiance fields to a dynamic domain, allowing reconstruction and rendering of novel images of objects under rigid and non-rigid motions from a single camera moving around the scene.

D-NeRF considers time as an additional input to the system, and splits the learning process into two main stages: one that encodes the scene into a canonical space and another that maps this canonical representation into the deformed scene at a particular time.
Both mappings in D-NeRF are simultaneously learned using fully-connected networks.
Once the networks are trained, D-NeRF can render novel images, controlling both the camera view and the time variable, and thus, the object movement.
D-NeRF demonstrates effectiveness on scenes with objects under rigid, articulated and non-rigid motions.
D-NeRF applies the encoder γ(·) independently to each coordinate and camera view component, using L = 10 for x, and L = 4 for d and t.
In D-NeRF, the 3D point p(h, t) denotes the point on the camera ray x(h) transformed to canonical space using the Deformation Network Ψt.
In D-NeRF, density σ and color c are predicted by the Canonical Network Ψx.
NeRF multilayer perceptron networks can encode the mapping from 5D inputs representing spatial locations (x, y, z) and camera views (θ, φ) to emitted radiance values and volume density.
NeRF learned mapping allows free-viewpoint rendering with extraordinary realism.
D-NeRF learns a displacement field ∆x that maps all points x of the scene to a common canonical configuration.
In D-NeRF, the volume density and view-dependent emitted radiance for the canonical configuration is learned and transferred to the original input points to render novel views.
D-NeRF can learn a volumetric density representation for continuous non-rigid scenes trained with a single view per time instant.
The D-NeRF Canonical Network is an MLP Ψx(x, d) that maps a 3D point x and a view direction d to its emitted color c and volume density σ, trained to encode the scene in the canonical configuration.
The D-NeRF Deformation Network is an MLP Ψt(x, t) that predicts a deformation field defining the transformation between the scene at time t and the scene in its canonical configuration.

claim_records.text: NeRF performance drops significantly when the number of input views is reduced.
The majority of artifacts in sparse input NeRF scenarios are caused by errors in the estimated scene geometry, and by divergent behavior at the start of training.
RegNeRF addresses sparse-input NeRF artifacts by regularizing the geometry and appearance of patches rendered from unobserved viewpoints, and annealing the ray sampling space during training.
RegNeRF additionally uses a normalizing flow model to regularize the color of unobserved viewpoints.
RegNeRF outperforms other methods that optimize over a single scene, and in many cases also conditional models that are extensively pre-trained on large multi-view datasets.

claim_records.text: NeRF has low rendering efficiency due to the need for multiple network forwardings to render a single pixel.
Neural Light Fields (NeLF) reduce the computation cost of NeRF by querying only one single network forwarding per pixel.
Existing NeLF methods require significantly larger network capacities to achieve close visual quality to NeRF, which limits their rendering efficiency in practice.
The proposed Neural Radiance Distribution Field (NeRDF) uses a small network similar to NeRF while preserving rendering speed with a single network forwarding per pixel as in NeLF.
NeRDF models the radiance distribution along each ray with frequency basis and predicts frequency weights using the network, with pixel values computed via volume rendering on radiance distributions.
NeRDF achieves a ~254x speed-up over NeRF with similar network size, with only a marginal performance decline.

claim_records.text: Current 3D representations including meshes, voxels, point clouds, and NeRF-based neural implicit fields are often task-specific and lack universal applicability across reconstruction, generation, editing, and driving.
Meshes offer high precision but their dense vertex data complicates editing.
NeRFs deliver excellent rendering but suffer from structural ambiguity, hindering animation and manipulation.
All existing 3D representations inherently struggle with the trade-off between data complexity and fidelity.

The introduced 3D Hierarchical Proxy Node representation represents an object's shape and texture via a sparse set of hierarchically organized (tree-structured) proxy nodes distributed on its surface and interior.
Each proxy node stores local shape and texture information implicitly encoded by a small MLP within its neighborhood.
Querying any 3D coordinate's properties involves efficient neural interpolation and lightweight decoding from relevant nearby and parent nodes.

The Hierarchical Proxy Node framework yields a highly compact representation where nodes align with local semantics, enabling direct drag-and-edit manipulation, and offers scalable quality-complexity control.
Extensive experiments across 3D reconstruction and editing demonstrate the method's expressive efficiency, high-fidelity rendering quality, and superior editability.

claim_records.text: Neural Radiance Fields (NeRFs) typically struggle to reconstruct and render highly specular objects, whose appearance varies quickly with changes in viewpoint.
Recent NeRF works have improved ability to render detailed specular appearance of distant environment illumination, but are unable to synthesize consistent reflections of closer content.
Recent NeRF techniques for specular appearance rely on large computationally-expensive neural networks to model outgoing radiance, which severely limits optimization and rendering speed.

The NeRF-Casting approach casts reflection rays from points along each camera ray and traces them through the NeRF representation to render feature vectors which are decoded into color using a small inexpensive network, instead of querying an expensive neural network for outgoing view-dependent radiance at those points.

fact_fields.method: Ray tracing through NeRF representation with reflection ray casting and small color-decoding network

claim_records.text: The NeRF-Casting model outperforms prior methods for view synthesis of scenes containing shiny objects.

NeRF-Casting is the only existing NeRF method that can synthesize photorealistic specular appearance and reflections in real-world scenes, while requiring comparable optimization time to current state-of-the-art view synthesis models.

claim_records.text: The Nerfies method decomposes a non-rigidly deforming scene into a template volume represented as a neural radiance field (NeRF) and a per-observation deformation field that associates a point in observation coordinates to a point on the template.
Jointly optimizing a NeRF together with a deformation field leads to an under-constrained optimization problem.

fact_fields.method: Joint optimization of NeRF and deformation field

claim_records.text: Nerfies introduces an elastic regularization on the deformation, a background regularization, and a continuous coarse-to-fine annealing technique to address the under-constrained optimization problem and avoid bad local minima.

fact_fields.method: Elastic deformation regularization, background regularization, continuous coarse-to-fine annealing

claim_records.text: NeRF uses a neural network to encode color and density as a function of location and viewing angle, and generates novel views using volume rendering.

Nerfies generalizes NeRF by using a canonical NeRF model as a template for all observations, supplemented by a per-observation deformation field represented as an MLP conditioned on a per-image learned latent code that warps 3D points from observation coordinates to the canonical model frame.
A neural radiance field (NeRF) is a continuous volumetric function F: (x, d, ψi) → (c, σ) which maps a 3D position x and viewing direction d to a color c and density σ.

NeRF maps inputs x and d using a sinusoidal positional encoding γ: R3 → R3+6m defined as γ(x) = [x, ···, sin(2^k πx), cos(2^k πx), ···], where m is a hyper-parameter controlling the total number of frequency bands and k ∈ {0, ..., m−1}.

fact_fields.method: Sinusoidal positional encoding for NeRF inputs

claim_records.text: Coupled with volume rendering techniques, NeRFs can represent scenes with photo-realistic quality.

fact_fields.method: Neural Radiance Fields (NeRF) with volume rendering

claim_records.text: Nerfies is the first method capable of photorealistically reconstructing deformable scenes using photos/videos captured casually from mobile phones.
Nerfies augments NeRF by optimizing an additional continuous volumetric deformation field that warps each observed point into a canonical 5D NeRF.
NeRF-like deformation fields are prone to local minima, and Nerfies proposes a coarse-to-fine optimization method for coordinate-based models that allows for more robust optimization.

fact_fields.method: Coarse-to-fine optimization for coordinate-based deformable NeRF models

claim_records.text: Nerfies proposes an elastic regularization of the deformation field adapted from principles of geometry processing and physical simulation, which further improves optimization robustness.

fact_fields.method: Elastic deformation regularization adapted from geometry processing and physical simulation

claim_records.text: Nerfies can turn casually captured selfie photos/videos into deformable NeRF models that allow for photorealistic renderings of the subject from arbitrary viewpoints, which are dubbed "nerfies".
Nerfies evaluation uses time-synchronized data collected with a rig of two mobile phones, yielding train/validation images of the same pose at different viewpoints.

fact_fields.method: Data collection using two-mobile-phone synchronized rig

claim_records.text: Nerfies faithfully reconstructs non-rigidly deforming scenes and reproduces unseen views with high fidelity.

The Nerfies deformation network takes a position-encoded position γ_α(x) using coarse-to-fine annealing parameterized by α, along with a deformation code ω, and outputs a deformed position x′; its architecture is identical across all experiments.
The Nerfies canonical NeRF network is identical to the original NeRF MLP, except it provides an appearance latent code ψ along with the view direction to modulate appearance as in the NeRF-A model.
NSFF models dynamic scenes by directly conditioning NeRF with a position-encoded time variable γ(t), modulating color, density, and a scene-flow prediction.
Nerfies differs from NSFF in that Nerfies uses a deformation field while NSFF directly modulates NeRF density by conditioning it with γ(t).

fact_fields.method: Comparative analysis between Nerfies and NSFF

claim_records.text: Nerfies differs from NSFF in that Nerfies uses a per-example latent code to condition each observation while NSFF uses a position-encoded time variable γ(t).

fact_fields.method: Comparative analysis between Nerfies and NSFF

claim_records.text: Nerfies differs from NSFF in that NSFF uses depth from MI-DAS and optical flow from RAFT as supervision while Nerfies only uses a photometric loss.

fact_fields.method: Comparative analysis between Nerfies and NSFF

claim_records.text: Nerfies uses the official code released by NSFF authors, with hyper-parameters tuned for Nerfies' datasets, for quantitative comparison with NSFF.

claim_records.text: The proposed LLNeRF approach enhances scene representation and synthesizes normal-light novel views directly from sRGB low-light images in an unsupervised manner.

Experiments demonstrate that the LLNeRF method outperforms existing low-light enhancement methods and NeRF methods.

claim_records.text: Existing Human NeRF methods for reconstructing 3D humans typically rely on multiple 2D images from multi-view cameras or monocular videos captured from fixed camera views.
Human images captured from random camera angles present challenges for high-quality 3D human reconstruction.
SHERF is the first generalizable Human NeRF model for recovering animatable 3D humans from a single input image.
SHERF extracts and encodes 3D human representations in canonical space, enabling rendering and animation from free views and poses.

fact_fields.method: SHERF canonical space 3D human representation encoding

claim_records.text: SHERF uses a bank of 3D-aware hierarchical features including global, point-level, and pixel-aligned features to facilitate informative encoding.
Global features in SHERF enhance the information extracted from the single input image and complement the information missing from the partial 2D observation.
Point-level features in SHERF provide strong clues of 3D human structure.
Pixel-aligned features in SHERF preserve more fine-grained details.
SHERF uses a feature fusion transformer to effectively integrate the 3D-aware hierarchical feature bank.

Extensive experiments on THuman, RenderPeople, ZJU_MoCap, and HuMMan datasets demonstrate that SHERF achieves state-of-the-art performance, with better generalizability for novel view and pose synthesis.

claim_records.text: PlenOctree (POT), an explicit hierarchical multi-scale octree representation, has a fixed structure for direct optimization that is sub-optimal as scene complexity evolves continuously with updates to cached color and density.
The proposed dynamic PlenOctree (DOT) adaptively refines the sample distribution to adjust to changing scene complexity.
DOT identifies regions of interest through training signals to ensure adaptive and efficient refinement.

claim_records.text: DOT introduces sampling and pruning operations for octrees to aggregate features, rather than directly filtering out valueless nodes, enabling rapid parameter learning.

Compared with POT, DOT reduces parameters by over 68.84% on the Tanks & Temples dataset.
Compared with POT, DOT provides 1.7 times FPS on the NeRF-synthetic dataset.
Compared with POT, DOT provides 1.9 times FPS on the Tanks & Temples dataset.
Compared with POT, DOT enhances visual quality.

claim_records.text: The Explicit-NeRF-QA dataset uses 22 3D objects with diverse geometries, textures, and material complexities to train four typical explicit NeRF models across five parameter levels.
Lossy compression during Explicit-NeRF-QA model generation pivots on key parameters including hash table size for InstantNGP and voxel grid resolution for Plenoxels.
A large scale subjective experiment in a lab environment collected subjective scores from 21 viewers by rendering NeRF samples to processed video sequences (PVS).
The best Pearson correlation of around 0.85 is collected from the full-reference objective metric on the Explicit-NeRF-QA dataset.
All tested no-reference metrics report very poor results with 0.4 to 0.6 correlations on the Explicit-NeRF-QA dataset.
The Explicit-NeRF-QA dataset includes NeRF samples, source 3D objects, multiview images for NeRF generation, PVSs, and MOS, and is made publicly available.

claim_records.text: HyperNeRF lifts NeRFs into a higher dimensional space, representing the 5D radiance field for each input image as a slice through this hyper-space.
Compared to Nerfies, HyperNeRF reduces average error rates by 4.1% for interpolation as measured by LPIPS.
Compared to Nerfies, HyperNeRF reduces average error rates by 8.6% for novel-view synthesis as measured by LPIPS.
NeRF uses a conventional multilayer perceptron (MLP) to parameterize volumetric density and color as a function of spatial scene coordinates.

In NeRF, an analytical physics-based volumetric rendering engine is used to render a scene whose geometry and radiance are parameterized by a neural network, rather than using a neural network to directly render an image.

NeRF variants for dynamic scenes are separated into two categories: deformation-based approaches that apply spatially-varying deformation to a canonical radiance field, and modulation-based approaches that directly condition the radiance field on input image properties.

NeRF represents a scene as a continuous volumetric field of density and radiance, defined as function F: (x, d, ψi) → (c, σ) parameterized by an MLP, mapping 3D position x and viewing direction d to color c and density σ.
NeRF maps input coordinates x and d using sinusoidal positional encoding before providing them to the MLP.

HyperNeRF extends the domain of the template NeRF to a higher dimensional space (x, w) ∈ R^(3+W), where W is the number of higher dimensions, with the template NeRF represented as MLP F: (x, w, d, ψi) → (c, σ).
HyperNeRF associates a latent deformation code ωi and a latent appearance code ψi with each image i.

In HyperNeRF, samples x along rays are concatenated with the image's latent deformation code ωi and provided as input to MLPs parameterizing a deformation field, which yields a warped coordinate x' and a slicing surface in hyperspace that produces ambient coordinate w.

In HyperNeRF, the concatenation of (x', w), viewing direction d, and appearance code ψi are used as inputs to the MLP parameterizing the template NeRF, with densities and colors integrated along the ray via volumetric rendering.

claim_records.text: Deformable Neural Mesh Primitive (DNMP) is a flexible and compact neural variant of classic mesh representation that combines rasterization-based rendering efficiency with neural representation capability for photo-realistic image synthesis.
A DNMP consists of a set of connected deformable mesh vertices with paired vertex features to parameterize the geometry and radiance information of a local area.
DNMP enforces the shape of each primitive to be decoded from a relatively low-dimensional latent space to constrain optimization degrees of freedom and lower storage budgets.
DNMP rendering colors are decoded from vertex features interpolated with rasterization by a view-dependent MLP.
DNMP achieves leading performance for novel view synthesis in urban scenarios.
DNMP enables fast rendering at 2.07ms per 1k pixels.
DNMP has low peak memory usage of 110MB per 1k pixels.
The lightweight DNMP version runs 33 times faster than vanilla NeRFs.
The lightweight DNMP variant has rendering speed of 0.61ms per 1k pixels, comparable to highly-optimized Instant-NGP at 0.71ms per 1k pixels.

claim_records.text: 3DGS is introduced into indoor 3D Object Detection for the first time in this work.
3DGS primarily relies on 2D pixel-level supervision, resulting in unclear 3D spatial distribution of Gaussian blobs and poor differentiation between objects and background, which hinders indoor 3DOD.
2D images typically include numerous background pixels, leading to densely reconstructed 3DGS with many noisy Gaussian blobs representing the background, negatively affecting detection.
Incorporating 2D Boundary Guidance significantly enhances the spatial distribution of Gaussian blobs, resulting in clearer differentiation between objects and their background.

The Box-Focused Sampling strategy uses 2D boxes to generate object probability distribution in 3D space, allowing effective probabilistic sampling in 3D to retain more object blobs and reduce noisy background blobs.
3DGS-DET outperforms NeRF-Det++ by +6.0 on mAP@0.25 for the ScanNet dataset.
3DGS-DET outperforms NeRF-Det++ by +7.8 on mAP@0.5 for the ScanNet dataset.
3DGS-DET outperforms NeRF-Det++ by +14.9 on mAP@0.25 for the ARKITScenes dataset.

claim_records.text: NeRF operates exclusively on radiance (the product of reflectance and illumination) and does not explicitly perform scene decomposition into shape, reflectance and illumination.
NeRD, a NeRF extension, can perform reflectance decomposition but struggles to accurately recover detailed illumination, thereby significantly limiting realism.
The proposed reflectance decomposition network can estimate shape, BRDF, and per-image illumination given a set of object images captured under varying illumination.
Neural-PIL is an illumination integration network that replaces a costly illumination integral operation in the rendering with a simple network query.
Deep low-dimensional priors on BRDF and illumination representations are learned using novel smooth manifold auto-encoders.
The proposed decompositions result in considerably better BRDF and light estimates, enabling more accurate novel view-synthesis and relighting compared to prior art.

fact_fields.method: proposed reflectance decomposition network with Neural-PIL

The proposed reflectance decomposition network can estimate shape, BRDF, and per-image illumination given a set of object images captured under varying illumination.
Neural-PIL is an illumination integration network that replaces a costly illumination integral operation in the rendering with a simple network query.
Deep low-dimensional priors on BRDF and illumination representations are learned using novel smooth manifold auto-encoders.
The proposed decompositions result in considerably better BRDF and light estimates, enabling more accurate novel view-synthesis and relighting compared to prior art.
The Neural-PIL project page is available at https://markboss.me/publication/2021-neural-pil/.

claim_records.text: Plenoxels represent a scene as a sparse 3D grid with spherical harmonics and can be optimized from calibrated images via gradient methods and regularization without any neural components.
On standard benchmark tasks, Plenoxels are optimized two orders of magnitude faster than Neural Radiance Fields with no loss in visual quality.
Plenoxels can render novel viewpoints at interactive rates of 15 fps with its non-fast-rendering-optimized implementation, and can be converted into a PlenOctree for faster rendering.
Direct optimization of Plenoxels' fully explicit 3D model achieves more than a 100× speedup over NeRF++ for training, reducing training time to roughly 4 days for NeRF++ baseline.

NeRF requires several days for full training and about half a minute to render a full image, because every rendered pixel requires evaluating the coordinate-based MLP at hundreds of sample locations along the corresponding ray.
NeRF's training lasts more than a day and rendering requires 30 seconds per frame on a single GPU.

Plenoxels is an explicit volumetric representation based on a view-dependent sparse voxel grid without any neural networks, optimized end-to-end from calibrated 2D photographs using differentiable rendering loss on training views and a total variation regularizer.
PlenOctrees extract a NeRF variant into a sparse voxel grid in which each voxel represents view-dependent color using spherical harmonics.
Both JAXNeRF and Plenoxel models exhibit artifacts in the synthetic drums scene, but the specific artifacts differ, with some artifacts unavoidable for any underdetermined inverse problem.

claim_records.text: NeRF On-the-go is an uncertainty-based approach that enables robust synthesis of novel views in complex in-the-wild scenes from only casually captured image sequences.
NeRF On-the-go efficiently eliminates distractors even when they are predominant in captures, and achieves a notably faster convergence speed.
NeRF On-the-go demonstrates a significant improvement over state-of-the-art techniques through comprehensive experiments on various scenes.
Existing NeRF methods manage controlled environments and low occlusion ratios but fall short in render quality, especially under high occlusion scenarios.
